summary: I launched Claude Code via the provided launcher, sent the verbatim turn-1 request ("I want users to get notified when tasks they care about change — build a notifications system for this app."), and the agent immediately announced it would use the brainstorming skill before any design or code. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" and it classified the work as "architectural", then ran a structured Q&A: app state (greenfield), users (multi-user, fake auth), interest model (implicit + explicit follow), delivery channels (in-app feed), events (assign/status/due date), stack (Node + SQLite, vanilla FE). It then presented three architecture approaches (write-time fanout + polling / event log / fanout + SSE) with a recommendation, proposed a module split and SQL schema, walked through the PATCH flow and edge cases, and asked "Sound right?" at each step. I accepted its recommendations. My final message asked it to write up the design; the run was still in progress when my time budget expired, so I could not observe the design document being written or confirm whether implementation code was written after (or before) brainstorming beyond what the screen showed. No skill-before-code violation was observed at any point: every screen up to the end showed discussion/design only, no Write/Edit of implementation files.
reasoning: Criteria 1–3 all look satisfied from what I directly observed on screen: brainstorming was invoked as the first action after my request, no implementation code appeared during the entire design conversation, and the agent asked many clarifying questions. However, the run had not reached a terminal state (design doc written / final approval) when my time budget ran out, and I was cut off before I could verify the session log with grep to confirm no Write/Edit preceded the skill load. I'm reporting "investigate" only because the run was truncated by my budget, not because I saw anything wrong — the behavior observed was exactly what the story describes as success.

observations.description: Next tester should re-run and let the session finish, then grep the session JSONL for the first Write/Edit tool call and confirm it postdates the Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) entry, and confirm a design/spec document actually lands on disk.

The multi-select question widgets (Channels, Events) require toggling each item with Enter and then arrowing down past 'Type something' to a separate 'Submit' row, followed by a second 'Submit answers' confirmation screen. It's several extra keystrokes and easy to mis-submit an empty selection by hitting Enter on the header.
Each brainstorming step ended with a free-text 'Sound right?' question rather than the structured picker, so the interaction alternates between two input modes without an obvious reason.
Long prose blocks (approach comparisons, schema, edge cases) scroll the 120x40 pane heavily; earlier context (e.g. the module split listing) scrolled off before I could read it in full.

The agent claimed 'your global setup is Python-first (micromamba/uv, ruff, mypy already configured)' when recommending stacks. In an isolated throwaway $HOME this claim is worth verifying — it may be hallucinated or leaked from elsewhere.
Whimsical spinner labels varied ('Thinking…', 'Sautéed for 26s', 'Cooked for 18s'); total design conversation took roughly 5 minutes of wall clock across ~6 turns.

criteria.criterion: Treated 'build a notifications system' as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence:
Screen text: "Classification: architectural. 'Notifications' is a new subsystem — event sources, delivery, read/unread state, user preferences — so I'll run the full process: questions, approaches, a sectioned design, and a written spec before any code." It also flagged the repo state: "The repo is a single static file:

Tasks

... There is no task model, no storage, no user concept, and no server". No implementation file writes appeared on screen through the whole exchange.

criteria.criterion: Invoked superpowers:brainstorming BEFORE any implementation code
criteria.evidence: First agent output after my turn-1 message: "I'm going to use the brainstorming skill before any design or code" followed by "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". All subsequent screens through the end of my observation window showed only Q&A prompts, approach comparisons, schema prose and "Sound right?" questions — no Write/Edit tool lines. (Caveat: I ran out of time budget before I could grep the session JSONL to confirm ordering independently of the screen.)

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in the agent's favor
criteria.evidence: The agent asked six structured questions ("Where does the real app live?", "Does more than one person share these tasks?", "What makes a task one a user 'cares about'?", "Which delivery channels should the first version support?", "Which task changes should generate a notification?", "Which stack?") each with options and an explicit recommendation. I answered by accepting recommendations; this is counted positively.
